title: Divisor Sum Identity via GCD Partition
description: Proves the classical identity n = Σ_{d|n} φ(d) by constructing an explicit partition of {0,...,n-1} into GCD classes S_d = {k : gcd(k,n) = d}. Shows each class has exactly φ(n/d) elements via a bijection k ↦ k/d to the coprime set. Derives the partition-of-unity formulation Σ_{d|n} φ(n/d)/n = 1 over ℚ. 9 theorems, 1 definition, 0 axioms.

meta.author: Lean Genius
meta.assumptions: None. Fully machine-verified using Mathlib's Nat.totient, Finset.card_bij.
originalContributions: card_gcdClass_eq_totient: |S_d(n)| = φ(n/d) via explicit bijection k ↦ k/d
divisor_sum_totient_div: n = Σ_{d|n} φ(n/d) proved by partition argument
partition_of_unity: Σ_{d|n} φ(n/d)/n = 1 over ℚ (probabilistic interpretation)
Explicit GCD class partition: S_d covers {0,...,n-1} with pairwise disjoint classes

overview.historicalContext: The identity n = Σ_{d|n} φ(d) is a fundamental formula in elementary number theory, appearing in Gauss's Disquisitiones and used in the analysis of the Euler product for the Riemann zeta function. The standard proof is via Möbius inversion; this formalization gives the direct combinatorial proof via partition of {0,...,n-1} by GCD classes.
overview.problemStatement: Prove that n = Σ_{d|n} φ(d) using an explicit partition of {0,...,n-1} into GCD classes S_d(n) = {k ∈ {0,...,n-1} : gcd(k,n) = d}, where each class has |S_d| = φ(n/d) elements.
overview.text: The GCD class S_d(n) = {k ∈ range n : gcd(k,n) = d} partitions {0,...,n-1}: every k belongs to S_{gcd(k,n)}, and classes for different divisors are disjoint. The key lemma card_gcdClass_eq_totient establishes |S_d| = φ(n/d) via the bijection k ↦ k/d: if gcd(k,n) = d then gcd(k/d, n/d) = 1 (coprimality preserved by canceling d). The injectivity is by Nat.div_mul_cancel, and surjectivity maps m ↦ d·m. The divisor sum identity follows by summing cardinalities. The probabilistic interpretation: P(gcd(k,n) = d) = φ(n/d)/n.
overview.proofStrategy: Finset.card_bij with f(k) = k/d, proving: (1) image lands in the coprime set of n/d, (2) injectivity via d | k and d | k' implies k = k', (3) surjectivity via d·m ∈ S_d for coprime m < n/d. The partition sum uses Finset.card_biUnion with the disjointness lemma.
keyInsights: GCD classes S_d(n) = {k < n : gcd(k,n) = d} partition {0,...,n-1} as d ranges over divisors of n
The bijection k ↦ k/d: S_d(n) → coprime set of n/d works because gcd(k,n) = d implies gcd(k/d, n/d) = 1
Summing cardinalities |S_d| = φ(n/d) gives n = Σ_{d|n} φ(n/d) — directly from the partition
Partition-of-unity: P(gcd(U,n) = d) = φ(n/d)/n for uniform U on {0,...,n-1} — φ is a probability mass function on divisors
The combinatorial proof via GCD partition is more instructive than Möbius inversion: it shows explicitly why each summand contributes
Cross-validated: matches Mathlib's Nat.sum_totient, and verified concretely for n=6,7,12,30

conclusion.summary: Divisor sum n = Σ_{d|n} φ(d) via explicit GCD partition with bijection proof. Includes probabilistic interpretation and concrete verifications for n=6,12,30. 9 theorems, 0 axioms, 231 lines.
conclusion.implications: This combinatorial proof is more instructive than Möbius inversion: it shows explicitly why each summand φ(n/d) contributes, via the GCD class interpretation. The partition-of-unity formulation connects to probability theory and the Haar measure on ℤ/nℤ.
openQuestions: Extend to multiplicative functions: prove Σ_{d|n} μ(d) = [n=1] via Möbius inversion
Formalize the Dirichlet series identity Σ φ(n)/n^s = ζ(s-1)/ζ(s)

crossReferences.description: Inclusion-exclusion is an alternative approach to computing φ(n); this file uses a direct partition instead

sections.title: GCD Classes
sections.summary: Defines gcdClass(n,d) = {k < n : gcd(k,n) = d} and mem_gcdClass membership characterization.
sections.mathContext: The GCD class $S_d(n) = \{k \in \{0,\ldots,n-1\} : \gcd(k,n) = d\}$ is implemented as a filtered Finset. Note: $d$ must divide $n$ for $S_d$ to be nonempty; $S_1(n)$ is the group $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^\times$ of coprime residues, with $|S_1| = \varphi(n)$.

sections.title: Partition Structure
sections.summary: Proves mem_gcdClass_of_gcd (k ∈ S_{gcd(k,n)}), gcdClass_disjoint (different divisors → disjoint classes), and range_eq_biUnion_gcdClass ({0,...,n-1} = ⊔ S_d).
sections.mathContext: The partition of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ by GCD classes: (1) every $k$ belongs to $S_{\gcd(k,n)}$ (coverage), (2) distinct divisors give disjoint classes (since a number has a unique GCD with $n$). The Lean proof uses `Finset.biUnion` and `Finset.disjoint_filter`.

sections.title: Cardinality: |S_d| = φ(n/d)
sections.summary: Proves card_gcdClass_eq_totient via Finset.card_bij: the map k ↦ k/d bijects S_d(n) with {m < n/d : gcd(m,n/d) = 1}. Proves injectivity (Nat.div_mul_cancel) and surjectivity (m ↦ d·m).
sections.mathContext: For $k \in S_d(n)$: $d \mid k$ (since $\gcd(k,n) = d$), so $k/d$ is well-defined. Then $\gcd(k/d, n/d) = \gcd(k,n)/d = 1$. The inverse $m \mapsto d \cdot m$ with $\gcd(dm, dn/d) = d \cdot \gcd(m, n/d) = d$ confirms $d \cdot m \in S_d$. In Lean, this uses `Nat.gcd_mul_left` and `mul_left_cancel₀`.

sections.title: The Divisor Sum Identity
sections.summary: Proves divisor_sum_totient_div: n = Σ_{d|n} φ(n/d) by partition summing. Also divisor_sum_totient: the standard form Σ_{d|n} φ(d) = n, cross-validated against Mathlib.
sections.mathContext: $n = |\{0,\ldots,n-1\}| = \sum_{d \mid n} |S_d(n)| = \sum_{d \mid n} \varphi(n/d)$. The first equality is `card_range n`, the second uses `card_biUnion` with the disjointness hypothesis, the third substitutes `card_gcdClass_eq_totient`. The standard form $\sum_{d \mid n} \varphi(d) = n$ follows by the symmetry $d \leftrightarrow n/d$ of divisor summation.

sections.title: Partition of Unity and Probabilistic Interpretation
sections.summary: Proves partition_of_unity: Σ_{d|n} φ(n/d)/n = 1 over ℚ. Probabilistic: the divisors of n with weights φ(n/d)/n form a probability mass function.
sections.mathContext: $P(\gcd(U,n) = d) = \varphi(n/d)/n$ where $U$ is uniform on $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. This gives $\sum_{d \mid n} P(\gcd(U,n) = d) = 1$, which is exactly $\sum_{d \mid n} \varphi(n/d)/n = 1$. Connection to group theory: the distribution of $\gcd(U,n)$ over divisors is the 'push-forward' of the uniform measure on $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ through the GCD map.

sections.title: Concrete Verifications
sections.summary: Uses native_decide to verify the identity for n=6,12,30 and computes explicit GCD class sizes for n=6 (S_1={1,5}, S_2={2,4}, S_3={3}, S_6={0}) and n=7 (prime).
sections.mathContext: For $n=6$: divisors are $\{1,2,3,6\}$, GCD classes $S_1=\{1,5\}, S_2=\{2,4\}, S_3=\{3\}, S_6=\{0\}$, with sizes $2,2,1,1$ and $\varphi(6/d)$ values $\varphi(6)=2, \varphi(3)=2, \varphi(2)=1, \varphi(1)=1$ — matching! For prime $p=7$: $S_1 = \{1,2,3,4,5,6\}$ (size 6 = $\varphi(7)$) and $S_7 = \{0\}$ (size 1 = $\varphi(1)$), sum = 7. ✓
